current_repo_note: The repository describes itself as maintained without human intervention; its philosophy document instead describes humans directing work through a chat channel while agents implement, its contributor guide is conventional, and recent commits carry a dozen human author identities with no automated account. Direct pushes to the main branch are policy-blocked and merges are performed by people.
canonical_data: in-workspace session files, worker state, and layered instruction files
strengths: Permissions are explicit and safe by default, with full access requiring a deliberate opt-in and a pre-dispatch enforcement gate
Every diagnostic command emits structured output, including build provenance and per-entry validation errors for tool servers and hooks
Runs against local compatible model servers, so it need not call a hosted interface at all
weaknesses: Its own maintainers state it is not the serious production project and direct users to two other tools to do real work
There are no releases and no tags at all, installation is build-from-source only, and the same-named package on the language registry installs a deprecated stub
The claim that it is maintained without human intervention is contradicted by its own contributor guide and by a commit history with a dozen human authors and no automated account
why_it_matters: A highly visible demonstration that agent-executed development can sustain a large codebase, and an equally clear illustration of the distance between that and a shippable tool.
